It is a drop-in replacement for `br` — every command, flag, and output format is identical — with one critical improvement: **concurrent claiming is correct**.\n\n---\n\n## The Problem It Solves\n\n`br` has a race condition at its core. Claiming a bead requires two separate operations:\n\n```\nbr ready --json          # read candidates (snapshot)\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <worker>\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr show <id>             # verify the claim stuck\n```\n\nWith 20 NEEDLE workers running simultaneously, multiple workers read the same candidate list, all select the same top bead, and all issue `br update`. SQLite last-writer-wins — 19 workers hold phantom claims on beads they don't actually own.\n\n`bf` eliminates this with a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` SQLite transaction:\n\n```\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --json\n```\n\nThe entire read-score-update sequence runs inside one write lock. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\nSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\n    │                                        │\n    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\n    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\n    ▼                                        ▼\n  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\n  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\n```\n\n**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\n\n**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\n\n---\n\n## Key Features\n\n### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\n\n```\nWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\nWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\n...\nWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\n```\n\nThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\n\n### Critical Path Scoring\n\n`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. Beads on the critical path (`float == 0`) receive a 1000-point bonus in the claim scorer, ensuring the fleet works on the most impactful beads automatically — without human priority curation.\n\n```\n$ bf critical-path bf-epic-123\n\n  float=0  [bf-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress\n  float=0  [bf-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\n  float=2  [bf-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\n```\n\n### Velocity-Aware Scoring\n\nWorkers declare their composition when claiming:\n\n```bash\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\n         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\n         --harness needle \\\n         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\n         --json\n```\n\n`bf` tracks close times per `(model, harness, issue_type)` in `velocity_stats`. The claim scorer weights candidates by `impact / expected_duration` — the fleet maximizes throughput per unit time, not just raw priority. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\n\n```\n$ bf velocity\n\nModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\nclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\nclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\nclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\n```\n\n### Atomic Batch Operations\n","numLines":100,"startLine":1,"totalLines":726}}}

= jsonl_issue.id.clone();\n498\t            jsonl_seen.insert(bead_id.clone());\n499\t\n500\t            match sqlite_issues.get(&bead_id) {\n501\t                Some(sqlite_hash) => {\n502\t                    if sqlite_hash != &jsonl_hash {\n503\t                        drift.hash_mismatch.push(bead_id);\n504\t                    }\n505\t                }\n506\t                None => {\n507\t                    drift.missing_in_sqlite.push(bead_id);\n508\t                }\n509\t            }\n510\t        }\n511\t    }\n512\t\n513\t    // Find beads in SQLite but not in JSONL (using tracked seen IDs)\n514\t    for bead_id in sqlite_issues.keys() {\n515\t        if !jsonl_seen.contains(bead_id) {\n516\t            drift.missing_in_jsonl.push(bead_id.clone());\n517\t        }\n518\t    }\n519\t\n520\t    Ok(drift)\n521\t}\n522\t\n523\t/// Count unflushed beads (db-only or db-newer beads not yet flushed to JSONL).\n524\t///\n525\t/// Returns the count of beads that exist in SQLite but have been marked as dirty\n526\t/// (modified or created since the last flush to JSONL).\n527\tpub fn count_unflushed(db_path: &Path) -> Result<usize> {\n528\t    use rusqlite::Connection;\n529\t\n530\t    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n531\t    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n532\t\n533\t    // Check if dirty_issues table |row| row.get(0))?;\n545\t\n546\t    Ok(count as usize)\n547\t}\n548\t\n549\t/// Get IDs of unflushed beads.\n550\t///\n551\t/// Returns a list of bead IDs that exist in SQLite but have been marked as dirty\n552\t/// (modified or created since the last flush to JSONL).\n553\tfn get_unflushed_ids(db_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n554\t    use rusqlite::Connection;\n555\t\n556\t    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n557\t    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n558\t\n559\t    // Check if dirty_issues table exists\n560\t    let table_exists: i64 = conn.query_row(\n561\t        \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='dirty_issues'\",\n562\t        [],\n563\t        |row| row.get(0),\n564\t    )?;\n565\t\n566\t    if table_exists == 0 {\n567\t        return Ok(Vec::new());\n568\t    }\n569\t\n570\t    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(\"SELECT issue_id FROM dirty_issues ORDER BY issue_id\")?;\n571\t    let mut rows = stmt.query([])?;\n572\t\n573\t    let mut ids = Vec::new();\n574\t    while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {\n575\t        ids.push(row.get(0)?);\n576\t    }\n577\t\n578\t    Ok(ids)\n579\t}\n580\t\n581\t/// Repair the database by rebuilding from JSONL.\n582\t///\n583\t/// This is the recovery operation when the database is corrupted or missing.\n584\t/// The JSONL file is the authoritative source of truth for repair.\n585\t///\n586\t/// # Arguments\n587\t/// * `workspace_dir` - Path to the workspace root (contains .beads/)\n588\t/// * `flush_first` - If true, flush unflushed beads to JSONL before repairing\n589\t/// * `force` - If true, proceed even with unflushed beads (they will be lost)\n590\t///\n591\t/// # Returns\n592\t/// * `Ok(usize)` - Number of beads imported\n593\tpub fn repair(workspace_dir: &Path, flush_first: bool, force: bool) -> Result<usize> {\n594\t    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n595\t        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n596\t    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n597\t    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n598\t    let jsonl_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.jsonl_export);\n599\t\n600\t    // Check if JSONL exists\n601\t    if !jsonl_path.exists() {\n602\t        return Err(anyhow!(\n603\t            \"Cannot repair: JSONL file not found at {}\",\n604\t            jsonl_path.display()\n605\t        ));\n606\t    }\n607\t\n608\t    // Check for unflushed beads if database exists and is valid\n609\t    // If db is corrupted, we can't detect unflushed beads - proceed with warning\n610\t    let (unflushed_ids, db_corrupted) = if db_path.exists() {\n611\t        match get_unflushed_ids(&db_path) {\n612\t            Ok(ids) => (ids, false),\n613\t            Err(_) => {\n614\t                // Database is corrupted or unreadable\n615\t                // We can't detect unflushed beads, so proceed with a warning\n616\t                if flush_first {\n617\t                    // Cannot flush from a corrupt database\n618\t                    return Err(anyhow!(\n619\t                        \"Cannot flush: database is corrupted and unreadable.\\n\\\n620\t                         Flushing from a corrupt DB would poison the JSONL checkpoint.\\n\\\n621\t                         Unflushed beads cannot be recovered.\\n\\\n622\t                         Remove --flush-first to proceed with repair only.\"\n623\t                    ));\n624\t                }\n625\t                // Proceed without unflushed check (db is unreadable)\n626\t                // No --force needed since we can't detect unflushed beads anyway\n627\t                eprintln!(\"WARNING: Database is corrupted and unreadable.\");\n628\t                eprintln!(\"  Cannot detect unflushed beads - any db-only beads will be lost.\");\n629\t                eprintln!(\"  Proceeding with repair from JSONL...\");\n630\t                (Vec::new(), true)\n631\t            }\n632\t        }\n633\t    } else {\n634\t        // DB doesn't exist - no unflushed beads possible\n635\t        (Vec::new(), false)\n636\t    };\n637\t\n638\t    if !unflushed_ids.is_empty() {\n639\t        if flush_first {\n640\t            // Flush ALL beads to JSONL first (not just dirty ones)\n641\t            // We must export everything because repair will rebuild db from JSONL\n642\t            eprintln!(\n643\t                \"Flushing all beads to JSONL before repair (including {} unflushed)...\",\n644\t                unflushed_ids.len()\n645\t            );\n646\t            let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n647\t            let flushed = storage.sync_to_jsonl(&jsonl_path, false)?;\n648\t            eprintln!(\"Flushed {} bead(s) to JSONL\", flushed);\n649\t        } else if !force {\n650\t            // Refuse to proceed with unflushed beads\n651\t            return Err(anyhow!(\n652\t                \"Cannot repair: {} unflushed bead(s) exist ({}).\\n\\\n653\t                 Run 'bf doctor --repair --flush-first' to flush before repair,\\n\\\n654\t                 or 'bf doctor --repair --force' to proceed (these beads will be LOST).\\n\\\n655\t                 Unflushed beads: {}\",\n656\t                unflushed_ids.len(),\n657\t                if unflushed_ids.len() <= 5 {\n658\t                    unflushed_ids.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\", \")\n659\t                } else {\n660\t                    format!(\n661\t                        \"{}, ... and {} more\",\n662\t                        unflushed_ids[..5].join(\", \"),\n663\t                        unflushed_ids.len() - 5\n664\t                    )\n665\t                },\n666\t                unflushed_ids.join(\", \")\n667\t            ));\n668\t        } else {\n669\t            // Force mode: warn but proceed\n670\t            eprintln!(\n671\t                \"WARNING: {} unflushed bead(s) will be LOST: {}\",\n672\t                unflushed_ids.len(),\n673\t                if unflushed_ids.len() <= 5 {\n674\t                    unflushed_ids.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\", \")\n675\t                } else {\n676\t                    format!(\n677\t                        \"{}, ... and {} more\",\n678\t                        unflushed_ids[..5].join(\", \"),\n679\t                        unflushed_ids.len() - 5\n680\t                    )\n681\t                }\n682\t            );\n683\t            eprintln!(\"Proceeding with repair due to --force flag\");\n684\t        }\n685\t    }\n686\t\n687\t    // Backup existing database if it exists\n688\t    if db_path.exists() {\n689\t        let backup_path = db_path.with_extension(&format!(\n690\t            \"db.backup.{}\",\n691\t            chrono::Utc::now().format(\"%Y%m%d%H%M%S\")\n692\t        ));\n693\t        std::fs::copy(&db_path, &backup_path)?;\n694\t        eprintln!(\"Backed up existing database to {}\", backup_path.display());\n695\t    }\n696\t\n697\t    // Delete old database\n698\t    if db_path.exists() {\n699\t        std::fs::remove_file(&db_path)?;\n700\t    }\n701\t\n702\t    // Create new database and import JSONL\n703\t    let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n704\t\n705\t    let result = storage.with_immediate_transaction(|tx| {\n706\t        import_jsonl(&jsonl_path, |issue| {\n707\t            Storage::create_issue_tx(tx, &issue)?;\n708\t            Ok(UpsertResult::New)\n709\t        })\n710\t    })?;\n711\t\n712\t    // Rebuild blocked cache\n713\t    storage.rebuild_blocked_cache()?;\n714\t\n715\t    // Clear dirty marks - after rebuild from JSONL, db and JSONL are in sync\n716\t    // (create_issue_tx doesn't mark dirty, but we clear for safety)\n717\t    storage.clear_dirty()?;\n718\t\n719\t    Ok(result.imported)\n720\t}\n721\t\n722\t/// Rebuild the blocked the same way a corrupted/partially-migrated DB does. `PRAGMA writable_schema`\n1428\t    /// lets us drop the NOT NULL from the table definition long enough to write the\n1429\t    /// bad row, then we restore it -- leaving a DB that is byte-for-byte what the\n1430\t    /// historical crash class produced.\n1431\t    fn inject_null_datetime(db_path: &Path, issue_id: &str) {\n1432\t        use rusqlite::Connection;\n1433\t        let conn = Connection::open(db_path).unwrap();\n1434\t        // Grab the current CREATE TABLE for issues and rewrite it without NOT NULL\n1435\t        // on created_at, temporarily, so the UPDATE below is accepted.\n1436\t        let create_sql: String = conn\n1437\t            .query_row(\n1438\t                \"SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='issues'\",\n1439\t                [],\n1440\t                |r| r.get(0),\n1441\t            )\n1442\t            .unwrap();\n1443\t        let relaxed = create_sql.replace(\n1444\t            \"created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\",\n1445\t            \"created_at DATETIME\",\n1446\t        );\n1447\t        assert_ne!(relaxed, create_sql, \"expected to relax created_at NOT NULL\");\n1448\t        conn.execute_batch(\"PRAGMA writable_schema=ON;\").unwrap();\n1449\t        conn.execute(\n1450\t            \"UPDATE sqlite_master SET sql=?1 WHERE type='table' AND name='issues'\",\n1451\t            [relaxed],\n1452\t        )\n1453\t        .unwrap();\n1454\t        conn.execute_batch(\"PRAGMA writable_schema=OFF;\").unwrap();\n1455\t        // Reopen so the relaxed schema takes effect, then null out created_at.\n1456\t        drop(conn);\n1457\t        let conn = Connection::open(db_path).unwrap();\n1458\t        let updated = conn\n1459\t            .execute(\n1460\t                \"UPDATE issues SET created_at = NULL WHERE id = ?1\",\n1461\t                [issue_id],\n1462\t            )\n1463\t            .unwrap();\n1464\t        assert_eq!(updated, 1, \"expected to null exactly one row's created_at\");\n1465\t        // Restore the NOT NULL declaration so the detector (which keys off\n1466\t        // PRAGMA table_info's notnull flag) sees a genuine NOT-NULL column holding a\n1467\t        // NULL value -- exactly the corrupted state seen in the wild. The DEFAULT is\n1468\t        // deliberately dropped on restore: SQLite substitutes a column's DEFAULT when\n1469\t        // reading a stored NULL, which would mask the very NULL we injected. schema_\n1470\t        // version must be bumped or the direct sqlite_master edit is discarded on the\n1471\t        // next open.\n1472\t        let restored = create_sql.replace(\n1473\t            \"created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\",\n1474\t            \"created_at DATETIME NOT NULL\",\n1475\t        );\n1476\t        let ver: i64 = conn\n1477\t            .query_row(\"PRAGMA schema_version\", [], |r| r.get(0))\n1478\t            .unwrap();\n1479\t        conn.execute_batch(\"PRAGMA writable_schema=ON;\").unwrap();\n1480\t        conn.execute(\n1481\t            \"UPDATE sqlite_master SET sql=?1 WHERE type='table' AND name='issues'\",\n1482\t            [restored],\n1483\t        )\n1484\t        .unwrap();\n1485\t        conn.execute_batch(&format!(\"PRAGMA schema_version={};\", ver + 1))\n1486\t            .unwrap();\n1487\t        conn.execute_batch(\"PRAGMA writable_schema=OFF;\").unwrap();\n1488\t    }\n1489\t\n1490\t    /// Regression for bf-3hm5h: a NULL created_at must NOT crash list/flush, and the\n1491\t    /// row must still load (as the Unix epoch) rather than aborting the whole Driving off the live schema (rather than a hardcoded\n/// list) keeps the detector and fixer correct as the schema evolves -- this is the\n/// \"generally\" in \"NULL-in-NOT-NULL rows generally\" (bf-3hm5h).\nfn not_null_columns(conn: &Connection) -> Result<Vec<NotNullColumn>> {\n    let mut cols = Vec::new();\n    for table in user_tables(conn)? {\n        // PRAGMA table_info columns: cid, name, type, notnull, dflt_value, pk\n        let mut stmt = conn.prepare(&format!(\"PRAGMA table_info(\\\"{}\\\")\", table.replace('\"', \"\\\"\\\"\")))?;\n        let rows = stmt\n            .query_map([], |row| {\n                let name: String = row.get(1)?;\n                let decl_type: String = row.get(2)?;\n                let notnull: i64 = row.get(3)?;\n                Ok((name, decl_type, notnull))\n            })?\n            .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;\n        for (name, decl_type, notnull) in rows {\n            if notnull == 1 {\n                cols.push(NotNullColumn {\n                    table: table.clone(),\n                    column: name,\n                    decl_type,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(cols)\n}\n\n/// Quote a SQLite identifier (table or column name) for safe interpolation.\nfn quote_ident(name: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"\\\"{}\\\"\", name.replace('\"', \"\\\"\\\"\"))\n}\n\n/// Detect rows storing NULL in a NOT NULL column (bf-3hm5h).\n///\n/// The schema forbids this, but corrupted databases have contained it -- most\n/// notably a NULL `created_at`/`updated_at` that turned every `bf list`/`bf flush`\n/// into a fatal `InvalidColumnType` crash. Reads are now NULL-tolerant; this\n/// detector surfaces the underlying rows so `fix_null_not_null` can repair them.\nfn check_null_not_null(db_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<NullNotNullViolation>> {\n    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n\n    let mut violations = Vec::new();\n    for col in not_null_columns(&conn)? {\n        // NOTE: test `typeof(col) = 'null'`, NOT `col IS NULL`. SQLite's query planner\n        // assumes a NOT NULL column never holds NULL and folds `col IS NULL` to a\n        // constant FALSE -- so `IS NULL` can *never* surface this corruption. `typeof()`\n        // forces per-row evaluation and reports 'null' for a stored NULL regardless of\n        // the column's declared constraint.\n        let count: i64 = conn.query_row(\n            &format!(\n                \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {} WHERE typeof({}) = 'null'\",\n                quote_ident(&col.table),\n                quote_ident(&col.column)\n            ),\n            [],\n            |row| row.get(0),\n        )?;\n        if count > 0 {\n            violations.push(NullNotNullViolation {\n                table: col.table,\n                column: col.column,\n                decl_type: col.decl_type,\n                count: count as usize,\n            });\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(violations)\n}\n\n/// Repair rows that store NULL in a NOT NULL column, in place (bf-3hm5h).\n///\n/// This is a non-destructive fixer -- unlike `repair`, it does not rebuild from\n/// JSONL, so it works even when JSONL is absent or itself suspect, and it never\n/// touches valid rows. Each NULL is replaced with a type-appropriate sentinel:\n///\n/// * `DATETIME` columns -> the Unix epoch (`1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00`), matching\n///   the value NULL-tolerant reads already substitute, so a fixed row round-trips\n///   identically to how it was already being displayed.\n/// * `INTEGER`/`REAL`/numeric columns -> `0`.\n/// * everything else (TEXT/BLOB) -> the empty string, matching the schema's\n///   `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` convention for text columns.\n///\n/// Returns the total number of column values updated.\npub fn fix_null_not_null(workspace_dir: &Path) -> Result<usize> {\n    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n\n    let violations = check_null_not_null(&db_path)?;\n    if violations.is_empty() {\n        return Ok(0);\n    }\n\n    let conn = Connection::open(&db_path)?;\n    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n\n    let mut fixed = 0usize;\n    for v in &violations {\n        let upper = v.decl_type.to_uppercase();\n        // SQLite type affinity: DATE/TIME columns first (they must not be caught by\n        // the INT affinity rule below), then numeric, then everything else.\n        let replacement = if upper.contains(\"DATE\") || upper.contains(\"TIME\") {\n            \"'1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'\".to_string()\n        } else if upper.contains(\"INT\")\n            || upper.contains(\"REAL\")\n            || upper.contains(\"FLOA\")\n            || upper.contains(\"DOUB\")\n            || upper.contains(\"NUM\")\n            || upper.contains(\"DEC\")\n        {\n            \"0\".to_string()\n        } else {\n            \"''\".to_string()\n        };\n\n        // `typeof(col) = 'null'`, NOT `col IS NULL`: the planner folds `IS NULL` on a\n        // NOT NULL column to FALSE, so an `IS NULL` UPDATE would silently match zero\n        // rows and \"repair\" nothing. See check_null_not_null for the full rationale.\n        let updated = conn.execute(\n            &format!(\n                \"UPDATE {} SET {} = {} WHERE typeof({}) = 'null'\",\n                quote_ident(&v.table),\n                quote_ident(&v.column),\n                replacement,\n                quote_ident(&v.column)\n            ),\n            [],\n        )?;\n        fixed += updated;\n    }\n\n    Ok(fixed)\n}\n\n/// Check database integrity.\nfn check_database(db_path: &Path) -> Result<(usize, bool)> {\n    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n\n    // Apply schema if database is new (no tables yet)\n    let needs_schema: bool = conn\n        .query_row(\n            \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='issues'\",\n            [],\n            |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0),\n        )\n        .map(|n| n == 0)\n        .unwrap_or(true);\n    if needs_schema {\n        crate::storage::schema::apply_schema(&conn)?;\n    }\n\n    // Run PRAGMA integrity_check\n    let integrity_result: String =\n        conn.query_row(\"PRAGMA integrity_check\", [], |row| row.get(0))?;\n\n    let integrity_ok = integrity_result == \"ok\";\n\n    // Count issues\n    let count: i64 = conn.query_row(\n        \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM issues WHERE deleted_at IS NULL\",\n        [],\n        |row| row.get(0),\n    )?;\n\n    Ok((count as usize, integrity_ok))\n}\n\n/// Check JSONL file validity.\nfn check_jsonl(jsonl_path: &Path) -> Result<(usize, bool)> {\n    if !jsonl_path.exists() {\n        return Ok((0, true)); // Empty workspace is valid\n    }\n\n    let mut count = 0;\n    let mut valid = true;\n\n    match stream_issues(jsonl_path) {\n        Ok(iter) => {\n            for result in iter {\n                match result {\n                    Ok(_) => count += 1,\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        valid = false;\n                        eprintln!(\"Invalid JSONL line: {}\", e);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            return Err(anyhow!(\"Failed to read JSONL file: {}\", e));\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok((count, valid))\n}\n\n/// Consistency drift details.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\nstruct ConsistencyDrift {\n    /// Bead IDs that exist in SQLite but not in JSONL\n    missing_in_jsonl: Vec<String>,\n    /// Bead IDs that exist in JSONL but not in SQLite\n    missing_in_sqlite: Vec<String>,\n    /// Bead IDs where content_hash differs between JSONL and SQLite\n    hash_mismatch: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// Check consistency between database and JSONL using content_hash.\n///\n/// Compares each bead's content_hash between JSONL and SQLite to detect drift.\nfn check_consistency_with_hash(db_path: &Path, jsonl_path: &Path) -> Result<ConsistencyDrift> {\n    use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\n\n    let storage = Storage::open(db_path)?;\n\n    // Build a map of all SQLite issues with their content_hash\n    let sqlite_issues: HashMap<String, String> = storage\n        .list_all_issues()?\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|issue| {\n            let hash = issue.content_hash();\n            (issue.id, hash)\n        })\n        .collect();\n\n    let mut drift = ConsistencyDrift::default();\n    let mut jsonl_seen: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();\n\n    // Stream JSONL and compare, tracking seen IDs\n    if jsonl_path.exists() {\n        let iter = stream_issues(jsonl_path)?;\n        for result in iter {\n            let jsonl_issue = result?;\n            let jsonl_hash = jsonl_issue.content_hash();\n            let bead_id = jsonl_issue.id.clone();\n            jsonl_seen.insert(bead_id.clone());\n\n            match sqlite_issues.get(&bead_id) {\n                Some(sqlite_hash) => {\n                    if sqlite_hash != &jsonl_hash {\n                        drift.hash_mismatch.push(bead_id);\n                    }\n                }\n                None => {\n                    drift.missing_in_sqlite.push(bead_id);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Find beads in SQLite but not in JSONL (using tracked seen IDs)\n    for bead_id in sqlite_issues.keys() {\n        if !jsonl_seen.contains(bead_id) {\n            drift.missing_in_jsonl.push(bead_id.clone());\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(drift)\n}\n\n/// Count unflushed beads (db-only or db-newer beads not yet flushed to JSONL).\n///\n/// Returns the count of beads that exist in SQLite but have been marked as dirty\n/// (modified or created since the last flush to JSONL).\npub fn count_unflushed(db_path: &Path) -> Result<usize> {\n    use rusqlite::Connection;\n\n    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n\n    // Check if dirty_issues table exists\n    let table_exists: i64 = conn.query_row(\n        \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='dirty_issues'\",\n        [],\n        |row| row.get(0),\n    )?;\n\n    if table_exists == 0 {\n        return Ok(0);\n    }\n\n    let count: i64 = conn.query_row(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dirty_issues\", [], |row| row.get(0))?;\n\n    Ok(count as usize)\n}\n\n/// Get IDs of unflushed beads.\n///\n/// Returns a list of bead IDs that exist in SQLite but have been marked as dirty\n/// (modified or created since the last flush to JSONL).\nfn get_unflushed_ids(db_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n    use rusqlite::Connection;\n\n    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n\n    // Check if dirty_issues table exists\n    let table_exists: i64 = conn.query_row(\n        \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='dirty_issues'\",\n        [],\n        |row| row.get(0),\n    )?;\n\n    if table_exists == 0 {\n        return Ok(Vec::new());\n    }\n\n    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(\"SELECT issue_id FROM dirty_issues ORDER BY issue_id\")?;\n    let mut rows = stmt.query([])?;\n\n    let mut ids = Vec::new();\n    while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {\n        ids.push(row.get(0)?);\n    }\n\n    Ok(ids)\n}\n\n/// Repair the database by rebuilding from JSONL.\n///\n/// This is the recovery operation when the database is corrupted or missing.\n/// The JSONL file is the authoritative source of truth for repair.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `workspace_dir` - Path to the workspace root (contains .beads/)\n/// * `flush_first` - If true, flush unflushed beads to JSONL before repairing\n/// * `force` - If true, proceed even with unflushed beads (they will be lost)\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `Ok(usize)` - Number of beads imported\npub fn repair(workspace_dir: &Path, flush_first: bool, force: bool) -> Result<usize> {\n    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n    let jsonl_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.jsonl_export);\n\n    // Check if JSONL exists\n    if !jsonl_path.exists() {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\n            \"Cannot repair: JSONL file not found at {}\",\n            jsonl_path.display()\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // Check for unflushed beads if database exists and is valid\n    // If db is corrupted, we can't detect unflushed beads - proceed with warning\n    let (unflushed_ids, db_corrupted) = if db_path.exists() {\n        match get_unflushed_ids(&db_path) {\n            Ok(ids) => (ids, false),\n            Err(_) => {\n                // Database is corrupted or unreadable\n                // We can't detect unflushed beads, so proceed with a warning\n                if flush_first {\n                    // Cannot flush from a corrupt database\n                    return Err(anyhow!(\n                        \"Cannot flush: database is corrupted and unreadable.\\n\\\n                         Flushing from a corrupt DB would poison the JSONL checkpoint.\\n\\\n                         Unflushed beads cannot be recovered.\\n\\\n                         Remove --flush-first to proceed with repair only.\"\n                    ));\n                }\n                // Proceed without unflushed check (db is unreadable)\n                // No --force needed since we can't detect unflushed beads anyway\n                eprintln!(\"WARNING: Database is corrupted and unreadable.\");\n                eprintln!(\"  Cannot detect unflushed beads - any db-only beads will be lost.\");\n                eprintln!(\"  Proceeding with repair from JSONL...\");\n                (Vec::new(), true)\n            }\n        }\n    } else {\n        // DB doesn't exist - no unflushed beads possible\n        (Vec::new(), false)\n    };\n\n    if !unflushed_ids.is_empty() {\n        if flush_first {\n            // Flush ALL beads to JSONL first (not just dirty ones)\n            // We must export everything because repair will rebuild db from JSONL\n            eprintln!(\n                \"Flushing all beads to JSONL before repair (including {} unflushed)...\",\n                unflushed_ids.len()\n            );\n            let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n            let flushed = storage.sync_to_jsonl(&jsonl_path, false)?;\n            eprintln!(\"Flushed {} bead(s) to JSONL\", flushed);\n        } else if !force {\n            // Refuse to proceed with unflushed beads\n            return Err(anyhow!(\n                \"Cannot repair: {} unflushed bead(s) exist ({}).\\n\\\n                 Run 'bf doctor --repair --flush-first' to flush before repair,\\n\\\n                 or 'bf doctor --repair --force' to proceed (these beads will be LOST).\\n\\\n                 Unflushed beads: {}\",\n                unflushed_ids.len(),\n                if unflushed_ids.len() <= 5 {\n                    unflushed_ids.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\", \")\n                } else {\n                    format!(\n                        \"{}, ... and {} more\",\n                        unflushed_ids[..5].join(\", \"),\n                        unflushed_ids.len() - 5\n                    )\n                },\n                unflushed_ids.join(\", \")\n            ));\n        } else {\n            // Force mode: warn but proceed\n            eprintln!(\n                \"WARNING: {} unflushed bead(s) will be LOST: {}\",\n                unflushed_ids.len(),\n                if unflushed_ids.len() <= 5 {\n                    unflushed_ids.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\", \")\n                } else {\n                    format!(\n                        \"{}, ... and {} more\",\n                        unflushed_ids[..5].join(\", \"),\n                        unflushed_ids.len() - 5\n                    )\n                }\n            );\n            eprintln!(\"Proceeding with repair due to --force flag\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Backup existing database if it exists\n    if db_path.exists() {\n        let backup_path = db_path.with_extension(&format!(\n            \"db.backup.{}\",\n            chrono::Utc::now().format(\"%Y%m%d%H%M%S\")\n        ));\n        std::fs::copy(&db_path, &backup_path)?;\n        eprintln!(\"Backed up existing database to {}\", backup_path.display());\n    }\n\n    // Delete old database\n    if db_path.exists() {\n        std::fs::remove_file(&db_path)?;\n    }\n\n    // Create new database and import JSONL\n    let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n\n    let result = storage.with_immediate_transaction(|tx| {\n        import_jsonl(&jsonl_path, |issue| {\n            Storage::create_issue_tx(tx, &issue)?;\n            Ok(UpsertResult::New)\n        })\n    })?;\n\n    // Rebuild blocked cache\n    storage.rebuild_blocked_cache()?;\n\n    // Clear dirty marks - after rebuild from JSONL, db and JSONL are in sync\n    // (create_issue_tx doesn't mark dirty, but we clear for safety)\n    storage.clear_dirty()?;\n\n    Ok(result.imported)\n}\n\n/// Rebuild the blocked issues cache.\n///\n/// This materialized view should be rebuilt after dependency or status changes.\npub fn rebuild_cache(workspace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n\n    let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n    storage.rebuild_blocked_cache()?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Reclaim stale in_progress beads.\n///\n/// Resets beads that have been in_progress for longer than the TTL\n/// back to open status.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `workspace_dir` - Path to the workspace root (contains .beads/)\n/// * `ttl_minutes` - TTL in minutes (default from config is 30)\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `Ok(usize)` - Number of beads reclaimed\npub fn reclaim_stale(workspace_dir: &Path, ttl_minutes: i64) -> Result<usize> {\n    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n\n    let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n\n    let reclaimed = storage.with_immediate_transaction(|tx| {\n        let stale_cutoff = chrono::Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::minutes(ttl_minutes);\n\n        let reclaimed = tx.execute(\n            \"UPDATE issues\n             SET status = 'open', assignee = NULL, updated_at = ?\n             WHERE status = 'in_progress' AND updated_at < ?\",\n            rusqlite::params![chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(), stale_cutoff.to_rfc3339()],\n        )?;\n\n        Ok::<_, anyhow::Error>(reclaimed)\n    })?;\n\n    Ok(reclaimed)\n}\n\n/// Initialize a new database from an existing JSONL file.\n///\n/// Use this to create a fresh database from a JSONL export without\n/// affecting the existing database.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `workspace_dir` - Path to the workspace root (contains .beads/)\n/// * `jsonl_path` - Path to the JSONL file to import from\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `Ok(usize)` - Number of beads imported\npub fn init_from_jsonl(workspace_dir: &Path, jsonl_path: &Path) -> Result<usize> {\n    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n\n    // Check if JSONL exists\n    if !jsonl_path.exists() {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\"JSONL file not found at {}\", jsonl_path.display()));\n    }\n\n    // Create new database and import JSONL\n    let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n\n    let result = storage.with_immediate_transaction(|tx| {\n        import_jsonl(jsonl_path, |issue| {\n            Storage::create_issue_tx(tx, &issue)?;\n            Ok(UpsertResult::New)\n        })\n    })?;\n\n    // Rebuild blocked cache\n    storage.rebuild_blocked_cache()?;\n\n    // Clear dirty marks - after import from JSONL, db and JSONL are in sync\n    // (create_issue_tx doesn't mark dirty, but we clear for safety)\n    storage.clear_dirty()?;\n\n    Ok(result.imported)\n}\n\n/// Verify database schema version.\n///\n/// Checks that all required tables and indexes exist.\npub fn verify_schema(workspace_dir: &Path) -> Result<bool> {\n    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n\n    let conn = Connection::open(&db_path)?;\n    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n\n    // Check for critical tables\n    let tables = [\n        \"issues\",\n        \"dependencies\",\n        \"labels\",\n        \"comments\",\n        \"events\",\n        \"config\",\n        \"metadata\",\n        \"dirty_issues\",\n        \"export_hashes\",\n        \"blocked_issues_cache\",\n        \"child_counters\",\n    ];\n\n    for table in &tables {\n        let exists: i64 = conn.query_row(\n            \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name=?1\",\n            &[table],\n            |row| row.get(0),\n        )?;\n\n        if exists == 0 {\n            eprintln!(\"Missing table: {}\", table);\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(true)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::config::init_workspace;\n    use crate::jsonl::export_jsonl;\n    use crate::model::{Issue, IssueType, Priority, Status};\n writable_schema`\n    /// lets us drop the NOT NULL from the table definition long enough to write the\n    /// bad row, then we restore it -- leaving a DB that is byte-for-byte what the\n    /// historical crash class produced.\n    fn inject_null_datetime(db_path: &Path, issue_id: &str) {\n        use rusqlite::Connection;\n        let conn = Connection::open(db_path).unwrap();\n        // Grab the current CREATE TABLE for issues and rewrite it without NOT NULL\n        // on created_at, temporarily, so the UPDATE below is accepted.\n        let create_sql: String = conn\n            .query_row(\n                \"SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='issues'\",\n                [],\n                |r| r.get(0),\n            )\n            .unwrap();\n        let relaxed = create_sql.replace(\n            \"created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\",\n            \"created_at DATETIME\",\n        );\n        assert_ne!(relaxed, create_sql, \"expected to relax created_at NOT NULL\");\n        conn.execute_batch(\"PRAGMA writable_schema=ON;\").unwrap();\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE sqlite_master SET sql=?1 WHERE .unwrap();\n        conn.execute_batch(\"PRAGMA writable_schema=ON;\").unwrap();\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE sqlite_master SET sql=?1 WHERE type='table' AND name='issues'\",\n String, bool) {\n    let out = bf()\n        .current_dir(ws)\n        .args(args)\n        .output()\n        .expect(\"failed to execute bf\");\n    (\n tmp\n}\n\nfn jsonl_path(ws: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n    ws.join(\".beads\").join(\"issues.jsonl\")\n}\n\nfn db_path(ws: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n    ws.join(\".beads\").join(\"beads.db\")\n}\n\n/// Run `git` .args([\"-c\", \"user.name=bf-test\"])\n        .args([\"-c\", \"user.email=bf-test@example.com\"])\n        .args([\"-c\", \"commit.gpgsign=false\"])\n        .args(args)\n        .output()\n        .expect(\"failed to run git\");\n    (\n        out.status.success(),\n        String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).into_owned(),\n        String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).into_owned(),\n    )\n}\n\n/// True when a usable `git` is on PATH.\nfn git_available() -> bool {\n    Command::new(\"git\")\n        .arg(\"--version\")\n        .output()\n        .map(|o| o.status.success())\n
